### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

When working with `custom_textobjects` based on treesitter queries (generated using `MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter()`, some languages do not work as expected.
Using the plugin `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` works as expected.

For example, the queries `@function.inner` and `@function.outer` work as expected in Lua, but not in Python or TypeScript (haven't tested more).
Pressing `vaF` in Lua selected the function, but in Python or Typescript when within a function gives `No textobject "aF" found covering region within 50 lines and `search_method = 'cover_or_next'`.

What makes the situation strange is when adding keymaps to the `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` plugin, this fixes the issue **after** running them. So for example (pasted below) when I press `vaG` to select the function first, this selects the function as expected. Running `vaF` **afterwards** also selects the function, running it **before** does not.

The same issue occurs not only in my example, but also when using the [MinMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax) configuration with Lua, Python and Typescript installed using `:TSInstall`.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-ai-treesitter' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-ai-treesitter/' on Unix

2. Inside 'nvim-ai-treesitter' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

   ```lua
   vim.pack.add {
     'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim',
     {
       src = 'https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter',
       build = ':TSUpdate',
     },
     'https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects',
   }

   require('nvim-treesitter').install {
     'lua',
     'python',
     'typescript',
   }

   require('mini.extra').setup()
   local ai = require('mini.ai')
   
   ai.setup({
     custom_textobjects = {
       F = ai.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = '@function.outer', i = '@function.inner' }),
       c = ai.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = '@class.outer', i = '@class.inner' }),
     }
   }) 
   vim.keymap.set({ 'x', 'o' }, 'aG', function()
     require 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects.select'.select_textobject('@function.outer', 'textobjects')
   end)
   
   vim.keymap.set({ 'x', 'o' }, 'iG', function()
     require 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects.select'.select_textobject('@function.inner', 'textobjects')
   end)
   ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-ai-treesitter nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Press `y` to install the plugins.

4. Create a new file `test.lua` in any directory and paste the following content:
   ```lua
   local foo = function()
     print('hello')
     local bas = 13
   end
   ```
5. Navigate the cursor inside the function body and press `vaF`. This should select the function syntax and body as expected.

6. Create a new file `test.py` in any directory and paste the following content: 
   ```python
   def foo():
     print('hello')
     bas = 13
   ```

7. Navigate the cursor inside the function body and press `vaF` as before. This shows an error message and does not select the function body. However, pressing `vaG` to call the `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` instead, selects the function body.
If you call `vaF` again, after running `vaG`, this also selects the function body as expected.

Demonstration:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f014869-98df-4466-8f3a-20b6f4058ad5

comment_data.body:
Hello @OptionalLion411,

Thanks for the issue!

This happens because `vim.treesitter` is not started automatically in the buffer. Using `:TSInstall` is not enough.

You can try this with the python example. Open the file, and type:

`:lua vim.treesitter.start()`

After that `vaF` works as expected.
I assume that `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` works a bit differently, starting `treesitter` if necessary.

Using minimax, the queries work immediately when you add the language to [this](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/da4d584b14966c49d5af41c79b98d460434f8e15/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L53) list.

You can also see [how](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/da4d584b14966c49d5af41c79b98d460434f8e15/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L43) treesitter is installed using `vim.pack`. Your example has a `build` property that is not supported.

Hi @abeldekat,
thank you so much for this great explanation and the very useful references!
I am new to Neovim and assume it is basic knowledge to start the treesitter first, but in case it's not, we could maybe add a sentence in the help documentation, since it works different than `nvim-treesitter-textobjects`.

> I am new to Neovim and assume it is basic knowledge to start the treesitter first, but in case it's not, we could maybe add a sentence in the help documentation, since it works different than `nvim-treesitter-textobjects`.

There is [already a mention](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/0f339bf5c93f392dc5d2417d47d7b9edc5f96fe8/doc/mini-ai.txt#L735-L737) that a tree-sitter parser should work (i.e. be enabled) for this textobject to work.
